 <alias ph="[ː]" contains="consonant"/>
 <alias ph="[ː]" contains="vowel"/>
</phoneme>

<stress>
 <placement contains="default">penultimate syllable</placement>
 <placement contains="nouns">on inflectional endings</placement>
</stress>
MSA.*Example:
qa[ː]lat - قالت
 sa[ː]fa - صفّ
 ba[ː]b - باب 
ʔa[ː]lam - أعلم
Stress falls on the penultimate (second to last) syllable by default: تَفَاحَة /tafāˈħah/ (apple)
MSA.Comments:
For nouns, primary stress can shift to grammatical inflections: كِتَابٌ /kiˈtābun/ (book)
So the length mark /ː/ does not change phonetically. It simply marks long consonants and vowels in Arabic.
Stress is not phonemic in Arabic but applies to syllables
Default is penultimate syllable
Stress shifts for nominal inflections

 <alias ph="[iː]" contains="default"/>
 <alias ph="[ɪ]" contains="unstressed-syllable"/>
 <alias ph="[eː]" contains="adjacent-to-pharyngeal"/>
 <alias ph="[~iː]" contains="shortened-casual-speech"/>
 <alias ph="[iː]" contains="word-final"/>
 <alias ph="[eː]" contains="before-pharyngeal"/>
 <alias ph="[ɪː]" contains="before-emphatic"/>
</phoneme>
MSA.*Example:
/iː/ as [iː] in default environments: سيارة /siːjaːrah/ (car)
/iː/ as [ɪ] when in an unstressed syllable: جِمال /d͡ʒiːmɑːl/ → [d͡ʒɪmɑːl] (beauty)
/iː/ as [eː] adjacent to pharyngeals: صِير /sʕeːr/ (became)
/iː/ as [~iː] shortened in casual speech: سيّارة [~siːjaːrah]
[iː] - عليّ (ʿalayy) 
[eː] - بيان (bayān) 
[ɪː] - ظيف (ẓīf)
MSA.Comments:
This indicates that /iː/ is realized as the long close front [iː] in most positions, but has these context-specific variants:
[ɪː] - long near-close [ɪː], before emphatics like ط ض ص
[eː] - long mid [eː], before pharyngeals like ح ع هـ
/iː/ has 4 allophones: [iː], [ɪ], [eː], [~iː]
Default [iː], [ɪ] in unstressed syllables, [eː] by pharyngeals, [~iː] shortened casually
